explanation: Conditional moves are instructions that perform an operation only if a certain condition is met.  They improve performance by avoiding the pipeline stalls associated with conditional branches. In pipelined processors, branches disrupt the flow of instructions, causing delays. Conditional moves allow the processor to continue processing instructions in parallel, even when the outcome of a comparison is unknown, leading to faster execution.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; CONDITIONAL MOVES (CMOV) - Avoiding Pipeline Stalls

; Traditional Branch (High Latency Risk)
    cmp r10, r11
    jg .L_Target         ; Branch: Flushes pipeline on mispredict
    mov r12, r13
.L_Target:

; Conditional Move (Pipelining Friendly)
    mov r12, 0           ; Setup default
    cmp r10, r11
    cmovg r12, r13       ; Move r13 -> r12 only IF Greater
                         ; No control flow change
                         ; Allows continuous instruction flow
                         ; Reduces penalty of unknown conditions
keywords: CMOV instruction, Branchless programming, Pipeline stall avoidance
